finding.claim: The /rss route fetches an arbitrary URL from the `u` query parameter with no host, scheme, port, or address validation, and returns the first 400 bytes of the response to the caller (full-read SSRF).
finding.source: app.rb:8 params[:u] (query parameter `u` on GET /rss, attacker-controlled, unauthenticated)
finding.sink: app.rb:8 URI.open(...) (open-uri performs the outbound HTTP(S) request and .read returns the body)

trace.note: .read fetches the full response body from the attacker-chosen URL
data[0, 400] returns the first 400 bytes to the requester, so the SSRF is non-blind

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. No host allowlist (TRUSTED at app.rb:5 is only used by /trusted). No scheme restriction. No port restriction. No private, loopback, or link-local IP blocking (for example 127.0.0.0/8, 10.0.0.0/8, 169.254.169.254). open-uri follows http-to-https redirects, so an allowed-looking URL can redirect to an internal target. No DNS pinning or rebinding protection. No authentication or authorization on the route.
finding.repro: GET /rss?u=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ returns the first 400 bytes of the cloud metadata response when run on a cloud host. GET /rss?u=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ reaches local-only services.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only host check is at app.rb:14, which belongs to the /trusted route and not the /rss path. TRUSTED (app.rb:5) is used only there. Nothing validates params[:u] on /rss before URI.open at app.rb:8, and there is no authentication on that route.
verdict.reason: app.rb:7-9 passes the unauthenticated query parameter params[:u] straight into URI.open, calls .read on the response, and returns data[0, 400] to the caller, so the SSRF is non-blind with no scheme, host, or address guard on the path.
